statusNote: starlight-changelogs and the publish-redeploy workflow are both spiked green; u9 is a notes-template wording choice a story can settle

unknowns.question: How do the release notes drop their '# 🚀 Ang vX: theme' h1 and move sections to ###, and where does the theme line go instead? A wording choice for Zac in releases/notes/README.md.

knowns.fact: The docs site is Astro Starlight in docs/, deployed to GitHub Pages by deploy-docs.yml, which runs on pushes to main touching docs/** or workflow_dispatch; dependencies are pinned and add-ons kept minimal.
Releases are drafts created by release.yml on a v* tag push from releases/notes/<tag>.md, rc tags marked pre-release, and Zac publishes each by hand.
No pagination: Ang expects few releases, so the page shows them all, newest first.

starlight-changelogs 0.7.2 (HiDeoo) is the only off-the-shelf Starlight plugin; all six real releases pages found use it, and others run it on Starlight 0.43.1 and Astro 7.4. It reads GitHub Releases at build time, always drops drafts and pre-releases, has no prose slot, and needs GITHUB_TOKEN in CI to avoid rate-limit 403s. astro-loader-github-releases is the data-only alternative (GraphQL, token required).
knowns.answers: How do other open-source repos and Starlight plugins build a releases page, and is there an off-the-shelf plugin that fits?

knowns.fact: Every surveyed site shows only a title and version picker above the list, no prose; starlight-changelogs offers no slot for prose.
knowns.answers: What sits above the release list: a header only, or some static prose? Let the survey of other repos show the done thing.

knowns.fact: starlight-changelogs 0.7.2 builds on Ang's Starlight 0.43.1 / Astro 7.4.12 only with an npm override pinning @ascorbic/loader-utils's astro peer to Ang's (otherwise npm nests Astro 5 and config load crashes); pageSize 100 gives one newest-first page; token reads from GITHUB_TOKEN; Ang's notes' '# 🚀 …' line renders a second h1 per release and their ## sections sit level with the version headings.
knowns.answers: Built on Ang's site, does starlight-changelogs behave as its source reads: one page with a big pageSize, GITHUB_TOKEN wiring, no doubled h1 from the release notes' own headings?

knowns.fact: RC pre-releases don't appear on the page (the plugin drops them anyway); it builds empty, title plus version finder, until v1.0.0 is published. Zac's call, 2026-11-23.
knowns.answers: Do release-candidate pre-releases appear on the page, and how are they marked?

knowns.fact: GitHub Releases at build time via starlight-changelogs' GitHub provider: drafts and pre-releases are filtered out and hand-edited bodies are what's shown; no file-based provider reads releases/notes/*.md.
knowns.answers: Where does the page's content come from: the GitHub Releases API at build time, or the releases/notes/*.md files in the repo? The files need no token but include unpublished drafts and miss bodies swapped by hand before Publish (the v1-launch-notes trigger).

knowns.fact: CI's GITHUB_TOKEN with contents: read does not see draft releases (tested 2026-11-23), so drafts can't break the starlight-changelogs build
knowns.answers: Does CI's GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: read) see draft releases? If so, any docs build between a tag push and Zac publishing fails, because drafts' null published_at breaks the plugin's schema.

knowns.fact: A deploy straight from release: published runs on the tag ref and github-pages rejects it ('Tag … is not allowed to deploy'); dispatching deploy-docs on main avoids it with no environment change
knowns.answers: A release: published trigger runs on the tag ref, and the github-pages environment only lets main deploy by default: add a tag rule, or check out main?

knowns.fact: A release: published workflow with actions: write running 'gh workflow run deploy-docs.yml --ref main' redeploys the docs when Zac publishes; deploy-docs.yml and the environment stay unchanged
knowns.answers: What makes the site rebuild when a release is published? deploy-docs.yml only runs on pushes touching docs/** or a manual dispatch, so the page goes stale unless a release-published trigger (or the file-based source) covers it.

decisions.decision: Build the page with starlight-changelogs 0.7.2's GitHub provider plus the npm override — only off-the-shelf option, works on Ang's versions in the spike, fits buy over build
RCs not shown; an empty page until v1.0.0 is fine — Zac, 2026-11-23
Redeploy on publish with a small release: published workflow that dispatches deploy-docs.yml on main — spiked green, no tag rule or deploy-docs change, builds from main's docs
